summary: CControls: hidden or disabled button can fire on a later mouse release
author: pm
body:
A CControls button whose parent is hidden or disabled stops receiving updates, but control_collection::handle_button_clicks still fires it if its last update saw a click, so it fires again on the next mouse release anywhere. Found while building the system menu (HH-0119): Apply re-applied the display when Keep or Revert was clicked. The menu works around it by giving a control one idle update before hiding or disabling it; other screens that hide or disable buttons are still exposed.

Proposed fix (author of HH-0119, unverified): in sources/ccontrols/control_collection.cpp handle_button_clicks, skip buttons that are not visible and enabled (effective, including parents).

**Done when:** the library skips hidden/disabled buttons, the sys menu workaround is removed or kept as harmless, and a check shows a button hidden mid-click does not fire on a later release.

Source: HH-0119 editor report, 2026-11-26.

**Verified, 2026-11-26:** throwaway harness 11/11 under MSVC and GCC (normal click, parent hidden/disabled mid-click, later release, toggle); Debug build clean; review PASS. The sys menu workaround stays (harmless).
